design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial in which "An independent epidemiologist generated a series of randomization codes for varicella zoster vaccine solution or distilled water based on a random number table," with 1:1 allocation of 54 participants to vaccine or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: A genuine random sequence (random number table) was generated by an independent epidemiologist with allocation concealed from administering staff via independent pharmacy personnel, and baseline age, sex, HbA1c and DPP-4 inhibitor use were similar between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "An independent epidemiologist generated a series of randomization codes for varicella zoster vaccine solution or distilled water based on a random number table. Independent research staff at the hospital pharmacy were then informed of the codes... The contents of the code were concealed by the independent research staff until the study was completed."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and administering/assessing staff were blinded with an identical-appearing placebo, both arms received concurrent PPSV23, all 54 randomized participants received their assigned injection, and the primary analysis was intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Pharmacists produced a vaccine solution or purified distilled water that were identical in appearance. A member of the medical staff was informed of the allocated participant code according to the order in the code table, but was blinded to the contents of the codes."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary skin-test outcome data were near-complete (52/54, with the two missing values imputed by last-observation-carried-forward), but the ELISPOT secondary outcome lost roughly 45% of participants per arm due to cell viability and exclusion of "high nonspecific reactions," with no sensitivity analysis to show results were unaffected.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In the ELISPOT study, contrary to expectations, the secondary outcome was insufficient because of the viability of the cells after thawing. We evaluated the values for the remaining 15 participants in each group both before and after vaccination, except for samples that revealed high nonspecific reactions."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective/validated laboratory and standardized skin-test measures applied identically at 0 and 3 months in both arms under double-blind conditions, so assessor knowledge of allocation could not plausibly bias measurement (though the skin-test cut-offs are reported with an apparent typographical inconsistency and inter-rater reliability is not described).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The reaction criteria were as follows: negative (score 0), < 5 mm; weakly positive (score 1), 5–9 mm; moderately positive (score 2), 10–14 mm; and strongly positive (score 3), ≥ 10 mm with double redness or induration reaction"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a pre-specified primary outcome and a priori sample-size calculation, but the protocol/registry entry is not available for verification and results are reported across multiple analysis sets (ITT and per-protocol) and several outcome operationalizations, with post hoc restriction of the ELISPOT sample, leaving some flexibility in the reported result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This trial was registered with the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, Japan (UMIN000004771)... The primary endpoints of cell-mediated immunity and safety analyses were used in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population, whereas the corresponding secondary analyses were used in the per-protocol analysis set."

overall_summary: This double-blind placebo-controlled trial had a robust randomization and concealment procedure, effective blinding, objective immunological outcomes and an ITT primary analysis, giving low risk in domains 1, 2 and 4. Overall risk is "some concerns," driven by substantial post hoc attrition in the ELISPOT secondary outcome (≈15 of 27 per arm analysed, without sensitivity analysis) and by unverifiable protocol details combined with reporting across multiple analysis sets; note also that the trial was powered for a 5 mm skin-test difference, so the null findings may reflect limited power.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial: "A total of 101 subjects... were enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two vaccination groups," with stratified enrollment and a registered trial number (NCT00322231).

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization with stratification is stated and the study is registered, but the sequence-generation method and allocation concealment are not described, and there is a notable baseline sex imbalance (70.6% vs 48.0% female) in a small sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 101 subjects, 50 years of age with a history of HZ 5 years prior to screening, were enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two vaccination groups. Enrollment in each group was stratified in an approximate 2:1 ratio by number of years since their episode of HZ... Subjects in both groups were generally comparable with respect to baseline characteristics (Table 1), except there were a higher percentage of females in Group 1 (70.6%) than in Group 2 (48.0%)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding with an indistinguishable placebo was maintained and only one subject withdrew before dose 2, but the marked reactogenicity difference could functionally unblind participants in a crossover design, and immunogenicity was analysed per-protocol rather than by intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Vaccine and placebo were reconstituted with sterile diluent immediately prior to administration, and were indistinguishable from each other." ... "The rate of reported injection-site AEs was higher in vaccine recipients (45.9%) than in placebo recipients (4.2%)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for essentially all randomized subjects (95–100% follow-up for safety; 95–97 of 100 for immunogenicity), with only a single consent withdrawal, so bias from missingness is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "100% (51/51) of the subjects randomized to Group 1 and 98.0% (49/50) of subjects randomized to Group 2 completed all study visits." ... "Subjects with follow-up 98 (98.0) / 96 (95.0)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The immunogenicity outcome (gpELISA titer) is an objective laboratory measure applied identically to both groups, but the primary safety/tolerability outcome relies on subject self-report and investigator causality judgments that could be influenced by reactogenicity-driven unblinding; specimens from the two varicelliform rashes were not obtained for PCR confirmation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Safety and tolerability were assessed by using a Vaccination Report Card (VRC). The subject recorded the maximum size (in inches) of erythema and swelling, and the maximum severity of pain or tenderness... The site investigator evaluated each AE as to seriousness, action taken, maximum intensity... and relationship to vaccine."

domain_judgments.rationale: Objectives were prespecified and the trial was registered (NCT00322231), but the full protocol/analysis plan is not available, a p-value is reported despite the stated absence of hypothesis testing, and multiple subgroup analyses (stratum and age) are presented, leaving some scope for selective reporting; the study was also funded and analysed by the manufacturer, whose sponsor "formally reviewed a penultimate draft."
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This was an estimation study with no hypothesis testing. The primary objective was to determine whether zoster vaccine was generally well tolerated... The secondary objective was to determine whether zoster vaccine was immunogenic..."

overall_summary: This registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial had near-complete follow-up and an objective immunogenicity endpoint, but it does not report the randomization sequence generation or allocation concealment methods, shows a baseline sex imbalance, and relies on participant-reported safety outcomes that could be affected by reactogenicity-driven unblinding. Combined with per-protocol immunogenicity analysis, unavailable protocol/analysis plan, and sponsor involvement in analysis and manuscript review, the study is rated "some concerns" overall, driven by four domains at that level with no domain reaching high risk.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial in which "Subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive 2 doses of either ZV or placebo, according to a computer-generated, study-center specific allocation schedule" (NCT00109122).

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was by a computer-generated, center-specific schedule prepared by an independent sponsor statistician with sequentially assigned allocation numbers and vial-level blinding, and baseline demographics/comorbidities were broadly comparable (a modest age imbalance, mean 68.7 vs 70.7 years, is consistent with chance and was adjusted for in the models).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive 2 doses of either ZV or placebo, according to a computer-generated, study-center specific allocation schedule... The allocation schedule was generated by a sponsor statistician not otherwise associated with the ZV program."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators and sponsor staff were blinded with careful procedures to mask vaccine/placebo turbidity, and nearly all randomized subjects received both doses; however, immunogenicity results were analyzed per-protocol rather than by intention-to-treat (one randomized subject excluded, analyses restricted to "subjects contributing to per-protocol analysis").
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The subject, investigator, clinical study site personnel, and sponsor personnel directly involved in the study were blinded... n = number of subjects contributing to per-protocol analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Immunogenicity was measured identically in both arms with validated central-laboratory gpELISA and IFN-γ ELISPOT assays (samples batched per subject), and safety was collected with a standardized Vaccination Report Card from blinded participants, making assessor influence unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "PBMC were frozen, stored in liquid nitrogen freezer, shipped encased in dry ice to a central laboratory... until testing in a validated IFN-- ELISPOT assay."

domain_judgments.rationale: Safety follow-up was nearly complete, but immunogenicity data were missing for a substantial proportion of randomized subjects at several time points (e.g., ELISPOT GMC at 6 weeks postdose 2 available for only 68/104 ZV and 72/105 placebo subjects) with no sensitivity analysis of missingness, although losses appeared similar across arms and largely due to dropouts/invalid assays.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "6 weeks postvaccination 2 | GMC | 68 | 42.9 ... 72 | 21.4"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT00109122) with clearly stated primary safety and immunogenicity endpoints, pre-specified power calculations and multiplicity adjustment, but the protocol/analysis plan was not available for verification and many secondary endpoints and time points were reported, with the study designed, executed and analyzed by the manufacturer.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary immunogenicity endpoints were the VZV IFN-- ELISPOT geometric mean counts (GMCs) at 6 weeks after each dose of ZV... In conjunction with the external investigators, this study was designed, executed, and analyzed by the sponsor."

overall_summary: Randomization and outcome measurement were well conducted (computer-generated concealed allocation, robust double-blinding, validated central-laboratory assays), but concerns arise from per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat analysis, appreciable missing immunogenicity data at later time points without sensitivity analyses, and reliance on an unavailable protocol with sponsor-controlled design and analysis. Overall risk is therefore 'some concerns', driven by the missing-data and analysis/reporting domains.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes "a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial" in which 38,546 adults aged ≥60 years "received either VZV vaccine or placebo," with an intention-to-treat population defined as "all subjects who underwent randomization."

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation produced near-perfectly balanced arms (19,270 vs 19,276) with virtually identical age, sex, race, EuroQol and functional-limitation distributions, and concealment is supported by a double-blind design with a matched placebo supplied through a central VACSP Clinical Research Pharmacy Coordinating Center, although sequence-generation mechanics are relegated to the Supplementary Appendix.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We conducted a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial at 22 sites, in which adults 60 years of age or older received either VZV vaccine or placebo." / "The demographic characteristics of the two study groups were similar (Table 1). The median age in both groups was 69 years"

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, site investigators and outcome assessors were blinded by an identical-appearing placebo, co-interventions (antiviral and analgesic use) were balanced across arms, the intervention was a single injection leaving little scope for non-adherence, and analysis followed a modified intention-to-treat principle with results reported as "essentially unchanged" when the excluded early cases were added back.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Efficacy analyses were performed with the use of a follow-up interval that excluded the first 30 days after vaccination and the modified intention-to-treat population" / "The rate of use of antiviral medication among subjects with confirmed cases of herpes zoster was similar in the two groups (87.3 percent in the vaccine group and 85.7 percent in the placebo group)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was minimal and balanced (0.6% withdrawal/loss to follow-up; deaths 4.1% in both arms, 793 vs 795), surveillance duration did not differ between groups, and active monthly automated telephone ascertainment plus closeout interviews that "did not identify any previously unreported cases" make outcome-dependent missingness implausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "More than 95 percent of the subjects were actively followed to the end of the study (Fig. 1) and completed a closeout interview... Only 0.6 percent of the subjects withdrew from the study or were lost to follow-up; 4.1 percent died during the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Case ascertainment used a prespecified hierarchical algorithm applied before unblinding with central PCR confirming 88.4% of suspected cases, identical surveillance in both arms, and pain measured with a validated instrument (Zoster Brief Pain Inventory) on a protocol-specified schedule; although the burden-of-illness endpoint rests on self-reported pain, participants were blinded to allocation, so differential reporting is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Before unblinding, each suspected case of herpes zoster was classified as a confirmed case of herpes zoster or as not a confirmed case with the use of a hierarchical algorithm that incorporated the results of the polymerase-chain-reaction (PCR) assay performed at the central laboratory"

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary endpoints, success thresholds and analysis methods were prespecified before unblinding and the published protocol is referenced, but the trial predates mandatory registration (no registry identifier given), the full protocol is not directly verifiable from the article, and there is heavy sponsor involvement in analysis programming plus an acknowledged "post hoc, subject-by-subject review of serious adverse events conducted by the writing committee," leaving minor concerns about safety-outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A data-analysis plan was completed before the data were unblinded for analysis." / "The prespecified criteria for the success of the vaccine with respect to the burden of illness due to herpes zoster required a VE_BOI point estimate of 47 percent or more and a lower bound of the 95 percent confidence interval greater than 25 percent."

overall_summary: This very large (n=38,546), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial shows low risk across randomization, deviations, missing data (>95% followed to completion) and outcome measurement (pre-unblinding PCR-based case confirmation with a validated pain instrument). The overall rating of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5: the analysis plan was prespecified but the protocol is not publicly verifiable from the article (pre-registration era), the manufacturer was extensively involved in planning, analysis programming and authorship with multiple authors holding Merck equity, and at least one post hoc safety analysis is reported.
